summary.title: PlanBench-XL: Evaluating Long-Horizon Planning of LLM Tool-Use Agents in Large-Scale Tool Ecosystems

details: Existing tool-use benchmarks assume fully visible, clean, reliable toolsets or one-shot retrieval, so they cannot test whether agents can plan long-horizon tasks when only retrieved subsets of a huge tool space are visible and retrieved tools may be broken or misleading.

PlanBench-XL: an interactive benchmark where agents must solve multi-step tasks by iteratively querying a tool retriever (input-conditioned = forward anticipation, output-conditioned = backward anticipation, or both) over a large typed tool library, inferring implicit intermediate sub-goals whose values are only obtainable through tool execution.

An optional retrieval-time blocking module hides path-critical tools by substituting explicit-error, silently-wrong, or semantically-misleading alternatives, while provably preserving at least one feasible solution path, forcing runtime detection of disrupted paths and re-planning.

Scalable LLM-based generation pipeline: typed datatypes -> executable tools with typed input/output schemas -> backend records -> queries whose solvability and ground-truth tool sequences are computed on a state graph.
Retail domain; 56 datatypes, 327 queries, 1,665 tools (185 executable + 925 noisy variants across 5 noise categories such as deprecated/stale/unreliable); ~25 turns per task on average.

Tools built by enumerating datatype-set pairs (1-5 inputs, 1 output), proposed by GPT-5.2 and filtered by GPT-5.2 for deterministic dependency, tool-grounded information access, domain realism, and non-trivial information gain.

Queries retained only if shortest valid solution requires >=5 distinct tool calls (L* = 5-9); ground-truth tool sequences enumerated as inclusion-minimal tool sets plus legal execution orders on the state graph; final answers generated by executing one gold path.

Runtime: actions restricted to retrieve / tool-call / answer, T_max=100 turns, at most 30 tools returned per retrieval (<=14 executable matches), datatype checks prevent answering without reaching the target typed state; answers scored by normalized containment matching.
Ten proprietary and open-source LLMs, including GPT-5.4 and GPT-5.4-Mini, Gemini-3.1-Pro and Gemini-3.5-Flash, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Qwen3-8B/14B, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct.
Temperature 0.0, max 8192 output tokens; open models served with vLLM, closed models via API; global seed 42 so all models face identical blocked tools within a setting.
Task completion: Accuracy, Executed Ground-Truth Datatype Precision (EGT Prec.), Average Turns.
Exploration: Mean Explored Datatypes (Mean EDT), Search-to-Call ratio, forward/backward retrieval ratio.
Execution quality: Invalid Tool Call Rate (ITCR), Untrusted Input Rejection Rate (UIRR, reuse of noisy-tool values as arguments).
Blocking severity: varying block ratio (fraction of feasible paths disabled); block type held fixed vs varied (explicit failure, implicit failure, semantically misleading, mixed).
Path-restricted blocking: only the shortest valid path preserved vs only the longest valid path preserved.
Inference-time augmentation: enforced-exploration prompts inserted whenever the agent tries to terminate with a wrong answer, up to a varying enforced budget.

Accuracy grouped by shortest solution length L*; error taxonomy of failed trajectories (No Traction / Irrecoverable Drift / Weak Recovery / Format Error), block-alternative follow-up behavior (Unused / Search Reused / Value Reused), and termination policies (Surrender / Wrong tool value / Search exhaustion).

key_findings.finding: Long-horizon planning over a large retrieval-mediated toolset is hard for frontier LLMs and collapses further when path-critical tools are blocked.
key_findings.evidence: Best model Gemini-3.1-Pro reaches 77.06% accuracy with 91.47% EGT Precision, while most models stay below 60% and Qwen3-8B and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct score 0%; GPT-5.4 falls from 51.90% in the block-free setting to about 30% when only one feasible path remains and 11.36% when only the longest recovery path is preserved.

key_findings.finding: Silent (implicit) tool failures are the most damaging perturbation because agents propagate their fabricated values instead of abandoning the branch.
key_findings.evidence: With blocked tools and block ratio fixed, implicit failures give the lowest accuracy of all single block types across models and the highest UIRR (11.99% vs 9.67% explicit and 9.89% misleading); implicit-failure outputs are reused as later tool arguments in 42.2% of follow-ups on aggregate (55.9% GPT-5.4, 75.5% Llama-3.3-70B) versus 0% for explicit-error outputs, while semantically misleading tools account for at most 3% of invoked alternatives.

key_findings.finding: The dominant failure is trajectory drift caused by tool selection rather than by failed tool discovery, and agents almost never recover after drifting.
key_findings.evidence: Irrecoverable Drift is the largest failure category (72.4% for GPT-5.4, 71.3% for Gemini-3.5-Flash) while Weak Recovery is only 3.0% aggregated; before a non-progress call the agent had already retrieved a progress-capable tool in 78.0% of default and 71.1% of block cases, 74.1% of default non-progress calls use tools from recent retrieval windows, and a progress-capable tool re-appears in recent context after drift in 42.5% (default) / 53.4% (block) of cases yet is still not selected.

key_findings.finding: Simply spending more test-time interaction does not repair adaptive re-planning failures under blocking.
key_findings.evidence: Enforced-exploration prompts that block premature termination, scaled over increasing enforced budgets, improve most models by less than 5 percentage points and leave block-setting accuracy far below the corresponding no-block accuracy.

key_findings.finding: Success requires bi-directional, accurate exploration plus reliable execution, not merely frequent retrieval, and each model family exhibits a stable characteristic termination policy after failure.
key_findings.evidence: Accuracy correlates with Mean EDT (r=0.902), relative frequency of output-conditioned (backward) retrieval (r=0.800), and EGT Precision (r=0.781), and negatively with ITCR (r=-0.443); Gemini-3.5-Flash has the highest S/C ratio (10.44) and most turns (57.87) yet lower Mean EDT than Gemini-3.1-Pro; on failures GPT-5.4 surrenders in 77.3% (default) / 80.6% (block) of cases despite guaranteed solvability, Llama-3.3-70B commits wrong tool values in 81.7%, and Gemini-3.5-Flash ends by search exhaustion in 90.8%, with these patterns stable across settings.
